fields.title: Monetization: how to increase customer revenue
fields.keyTakeaway: Customer lifetime revenue grows through four levers: price, retention, expansion, and pricing structure. Price is the fastest and most intimidating lever, while account expansion is usually the cheapest.
fields.checkQuestion: What happens to LTV if you raise prices by 15% and churn 5% of clients?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **how to increase LTV?**
fields.blocks/1/subtitle: Adjust one at a time, otherwise you cannot isolate the impact
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **Price** — direct and underrated. A modest price hike almost never triggers a proportional churn spike.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **Retention** — every additional month of client lifetime adds a full subscription check.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **Expansion** — more warehouses, more seats, add-on modules. Upselling an existing customer is cheaper than acquiring a new one.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **Pricing structure** — the value metric charged for. The pricing metric should scale alongside the value delivered to the client.
fields.blocks/2/text:
Current state: 120 clients × 40,000 ₽ = 4.8 million ₽ per month.

A 15% price increase with 5% customer churn:
114 × 46,000 = 5.24 million ₽. Revenue increases by +9%, while supporting six fewer clients.

For the price hike to be net-negative, churn would need to exceed 13% — whereas market benchmarks show a 3–6% churn for a 15% increase.

Caution: evaluate by customer segment. Retail chains have different price elasticity, while for micro-clients 15% might hit budget hard caps.
fields.blocks/2/title: Kedr: the math behind a price hike
fields.blocks/3/text: **The value metric matters more than price point.** If Kedr charges per seat, clients optimize by sharing a single login — costing you both revenue and data hygiene. If you charge per warehouse location or shipment volume, billings naturally scale with delivered value without friction.
fields.blocks/4/text: You can raise prices for new sign-ups tomorrow. Existing clients require advance notice, clear rationale, and often grandfathering options. Price discrimination between new and legacy accounts is standard practice.
fields.blocks/4/title: Price increases for legacy clients require a dedicated plan
fields.blocks/5/text: Monetization levers work only when the core product actually solves the user's problem. Raising prices on a leaky product accelerates churn and skews elasticity data.
